beats.say: Isha has 5 bags of rice. Each bag weighs 8 kilograms 500 grams. We want the weight of all the bags, in grams.

board.text: 5 bags, each 8 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: Each bag's weight mixes two units, kilograms and grams. What is a good first step?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 8 kilograms is 8000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 8500 grams. Careful: 8500 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 5 bags, so we need 8500 times 5. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 8000 times 5?

ask.ifNot: Work out 8 times 5 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 8000 times 5 is 40000. And 500 times 5 is 2500.
Put the two parts together. 40000 plus 2500 makes 42500. So the 5 bags weigh 42500 grams.
The plan to remember: change everything into the small unit first, then multiply.
Here are 2 bags of sugar, and each one weighs 5 kilograms 750 grams. Our job is to find the total weight in grams.

board.text: 2 bags, each 5 kg 750 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: We want grams at the end. Right now each bag is in kilograms and grams. Where shall we begin?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 5 kilograms is 5000 grams.
Now add on the 750 grams. One bag weighs 5750 grams. Don't stop here, though. 5750 is just one bag, and it is sitting in the choices to catch us.
There are 2 bags, so we need 5750 times 2. That is doubling. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 5000 times 2?

ask.ifNot: Work out 5 times 2 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 5000 times 2 is 10000. And 750 times 2 is 1500.
Put the two parts together. 10000 plus 1500 makes 11500. So the 2 bags weigh 11500 grams.
The plan to remember: change everything into the small unit first, then multiply.
Here are 4 bags of sugar, and each one weighs 3 kilograms 500 grams. Our job is to find the total weight in grams.

board.text: 4 bags, each 3 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: The answer has to be in grams, but each bag is given in kilograms and grams. So what shall we do first?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 3 kilograms is 3000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 3500 grams. Don't stop here, though. 3500 is just one bag, and it is sitting in the choices to catch us.
There are 4 bags, so we need 3500 times 4. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 3000 times 4?

ask.ifNot: Work out 3 times 4 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 3000 times 4 is 12000. And 500 times 4 is 2000.
Put the two parts together. 12000 plus 2000 makes 14000. So the 4 bags weigh 14000 grams.
Two steps did it: one bag into grams, then times the number of bags. You can use that every time.
Here are 2 bags of wheat, and each one weighs 2 kilograms 750 grams. Our job is to find the total weight in grams.

board.text: 2 bags, each 2 kg 750 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: We want grams at the end. Right now each bag is in kilograms and grams. Where shall we begin?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 2 kilograms is 2000 grams.
Now add on the 750 grams. One bag weighs 2750 grams. Careful: 2750 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 2 bags, so we need 2750 times 2. That is doubling. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 2000 times 2?

ask.ifNot: Work out 2 times 2 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 2000 times 2 is 4000. And 750 times 2 is 1500.
Put the two parts together. 4000 plus 1500 makes 5500. So the 2 bags weigh 5500 grams.
Two steps did it: one bag into grams, then times the number of bags. You can use that every time.
Riya has 3 bags of flour. Each bag weighs 5 kilograms 500 grams. We want the weight of all the bags, in grams.

board.text: 3 bags, each 5 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: Each bag's weight mixes two units, kilograms and grams. What is a good first step?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 5 kilograms is 5000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 5500 grams. Careful: 5500 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 3 bags, so we need 5500 times 3. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 5000 times 3?

ask.ifNot: Work out 5 times 3 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 5000 times 3 is 15000. And 500 times 3 is 1500.
Put the two parts together. 15000 plus 1500 makes 16500. So the 3 bags weigh 16500 grams.
The plan to remember: change everything into the small unit first, then multiply.
Kavya has 2 bags of sugar. Each bag weighs 3 kilograms 500 grams. We want the weight of all the bags, in grams.

board.text: 2 bags, each 3 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: We want grams at the end. Right now each bag is in kilograms and grams. Where shall we begin?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 3 kilograms is 3000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 3500 grams. Don't stop here, though. 3500 is just one bag, and it is sitting in the choices to catch us.
There are 2 bags, so we need 3500 times 2. That is doubling. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 3000 times 2?

ask.ifNot: Work out 3 times 2 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 3000 times 2 is 6000. And 500 times 2 is 1000.
Put the two parts together. 6000 plus 1000 makes 7000. So the 2 bags weigh 7000 grams.
So when kilograms and grams are mixed, make it all grams first. Then multiply by the number of bags.
A gold ring weighs 5 grams and 15 milligrams. We want to write that as one decimal number of grams.
The 5 grams are already grams, so they stay. Only the 15 milligrams need changing. How many milligrams make 1 gram?

ask.ifNot: Milli means a thousandth. So it takes 1000 milligrams to make 1 gram.

beats.say: 1000 milligrams make 1 gram. So to turn milligrams into grams, we divide by 1000.
15 divided by 1000. Dividing by 1000 slides each digit 3 places to the right. So we get 0.015.
Careful here: it is 0.015, not 0.15. Thousandths need 3 places after the point, so a 0 has to stand in front of the 15.
Now join it to the 5 whole grams. 5 plus 0.015 is 5.015.
So the ring weighs 5.015 grams.
Remember: milligrams to grams means 3 decimal places. Fill any empty place with a 0.
We have to add 2 metres, 2 decimetres and 15 centimetres. Three lengths, in three different units.
Can we just add 2 and 2 and 15? Not yet. What must we do first?

ask.ifNot: Lengths can only be added when they are in the same unit. The choices are in centimetres, so let's change everything into centimetres.

beats.say: Start with the metres. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so 2 metres is 200 centimetres.
Now the decimetres. A decimetre is 10 centimetres, so 2 decimetres is 20 centimetres.
The 15 centimetres are already centimetres. Now everything matches, so we can add. 200 plus 20 is 220.
And 15 more makes 235. So the total is 235 centimetres.
Remember: same units first, then add. Never just push the numbers together.
Each bean weighs 2.5 grams, and the whole bag of beans weighs 0.5 kilograms. How many beans are inside?

board.text: Bean: 2.5 g. Bag: 0.5 kg. How many beans?

beats.say: One weight is in grams and the other is in kilograms. What do we do first?

ask.ifNot: We can only compare weights that are in the same unit. Let's change the bag's weight into grams.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. 0.5 means a half, and half of 1000 is 500. So the bag weighs 500 grams.
Now, 2.5 is an awkward number to divide by. Here is a trick: take 2 beans together. 2.5 plus 2.5 is 5 grams.
So every pair of beans weighs 5 grams. How many 5s are there in 500?

ask.ifNot: 5 goes into 5 once. So into 500 it goes 100 times.

beats.say: 500 divided by 5 is 100. That is 100 pairs of beans.
Careful: 100 is the number of pairs, not beans. Each pair is 2 beans, so we double it. 200 beans.
Check: 200 beans at 2.5 grams each is 500 grams. It fits. Same units first, then count how many fit.
We have 11 kilograms and 11 grams. We want to write it as one decimal number of kilograms.
The 11 kilograms stay as they are. It is the 11 grams we must change. A gram is what part of a kilogram?

ask.ifNot: Kilo means a thousand. So 1 gram is one thousandth of a kilogram.

beats.say: 1000 grams make 1 kilogram. So we divide the grams by 1000.
11 divided by 1000 is 0.011. Thousandths take 3 places after the point, so a 0 stands in front of the 11.
Here is the trap. 0.11 kilograms would be 110 grams, far more than our 11 grams.
Now join it to the 11 whole kilograms. 11 plus 0.011 is 11.011.
So the weight is 11.011 kilograms.
Remember: grams to kilograms means 3 decimal places. Fill the empty place with a 0.
4 mangoes give 250 millilitres of juice. We want enough juice to make 1 decalitre. How many mangoes is that?
First, that unusual word. What do you think deca means?

ask.ifNot: Deca means ten, as in a decade, which is ten years. Deci, with an i, is the one that means a tenth.

beats.say: So 1 decalitre is 10 litres. Each litre is 1000 millilitres, so that is 10000 millilitres.
Now, how many lots of 250 fit in 10000? Start small: 4 lots of 250 make 1000, which is 1 litre.
We have 10 litres, so that is 10 times 4 lots. 40 lots of 250 millilitres.
Careful now. 40 is the number of lots, and it is one of the choices. But how many mangoes does each lot need?

ask.ifNot: Go back to the start of the question. It takes 4 mangoes to make each 250 millilitres.

beats.say: Each lot needs 4 mangoes. 40 times 4 is 160. So we need 160 mangoes.
The plan: change to the same unit, count the lots, then multiply by the mangoes in each lot.
We must add 100 decigrams and 300 decagrams, and give the answer in grams. Look closely: the two words are nearly the same.
Deci, with an i. Is a decigram bigger or smaller than a gram?

choices: smaller: a tenth of a gram
ask.ifNot: Deci means a tenth, like a decimal. So a decigram is a small piece: one tenth of a gram.

beats.say: 10 decigrams make 1 gram. So 100 decigrams is 100 divided by 10, which is 10 grams.
Deca, with an a, means ten. So 1 decagram is 10 grams, and 300 decagrams is 300 times 10. That is 3000 grams.
Now both are in grams, so we can add. 10 plus 3000 is 3010 grams.
Look at the choices: 310, 3100, 3000, or none of these. Is 3010 there?

ask.ifNot: Read each choice digit by digit. 3010 has its 1 in the tens place. None of the numbers matches it.

beats.say: 3010 is not one of the numbers. So the answer is: none of these. Our working is sound, so we can trust it.
Remember: deci is a tenth, deca is ten. One little letter changes everything.
A shopkeeper sells 1 gross of eggs for 864 rupees. We want the cost of 1 score of eggs.
Gross and score are old names for numbers. A gross is 12 dozen, and a dozen is 12. So a gross is 12 times 12, which is 144.
And how many is a score?

ask.ifNot: A score is 20. A dozen is the one that is 12.

beats.say: So 144 eggs cost 864 rupees, and we want the price of 20 eggs. First we find the price of 1 egg.
144 times 5 is 720. One more 144 makes 864. So that is 6 lots, and 1 egg costs 6 rupees.
Now 20 eggs. 20 times 6 is 120.
So 1 score of eggs costs 120 rupees.
The plan: turn the number words into numbers, find the price of 1, then multiply.
We need to change 29 decametres into centimetres. That is a big unit going to a small one.
Let's go one step at a time. Deca means ten. So 1 decametre is how many metres?

ask.ifNot: Deca means ten. So 1 decametre is 10 metres.

beats.say: So 29 decametres is 29 times 10, which is 290 metres.
Careful: 290 is one of the choices, but that is in metres. We are not finished.
Each metre is 100 centimetres. So we multiply 290 by 100: two more zeros go on the end.
So 29 decametres is 29000 centimetres.
Going to a smaller unit, the number gets bigger. Times 10, then times 100, is times 1000 in all.
1 score of oranges costs 130 rupees, and 1 dozen apples cost 180 rupees. We buy 12 oranges and 17 apples. What is the bill?
A dozen is 12. How many is a score?

ask.ifNot: A score is 20. So 20 oranges cost 130 rupees.

beats.say: 20 oranges cost 130 rupees. So 1 orange costs 130 divided by 20, which is 6.5 rupees. 6 and a half.
We buy 12 oranges. 12 times 6 is 72, and 12 halves are 6 more. So the oranges cost 78 rupees.
Now the apples. 12 apples cost 180 rupees, so 1 apple costs 180 divided by 12. That is 15 rupees.
We buy 17 apples. 17 times 10 is 170, and 17 times 5 is 85. Together, 255 rupees.
Add the two costs. 78 plus 255 is 333 rupees.
Now look at the choices: 349.50, 356.50, 330, or None. Is 333 there?

choices: no, so the answer is None
ask.ifNot: Close is not the same as equal. 333 is not on the list, so we pick None.

beats.say: 333 rupees is not listed, so the answer is None. When your working is careful, trust it.
The plan: find the price of 1 of each fruit, multiply by how many we buy, then add.
160 hectograms of rice are shared equally among 25 people. How many grams does each person get?
Hecto is the new word here. What does hecto mean?

ask.ifNot: Hecto means a hundred. Deca is ten, and kilo is a thousand.

beats.say: So 1 hectogram is 100 grams. And 160 hectograms is 160 times 100, which is 16000 grams.
Now share 16000 grams among 25 people. Here is a neat trick: there are 4 lots of 25 in every 100.
16000 is 160 hundreds. Each hundred gives 4 lots of 25, so we need 160 times 4. That is 640.
Each person gets 640 grams. The choices are 680, 720, 600, or none of these. Which do we pick?

ask.ifNot: 640 is not on the list, and close does not count. So we choose none of these.

beats.say: 640 grams is not listed, so the answer is: none of these.
Check: 25 times 640 is 16000. It works. Change the unit first, then share.
A cycle track is 4 kilometres 75 metres long. We want that as one number of kilometres.
The 4 kilometres stay put. The 75 metres must become a part of a kilometre. How many metres make 1 kilometre?

ask.ifNot: Kilo means a thousand. So it takes 1000 metres to make 1 kilometre.

beats.say: 1000 metres make 1 kilometre, so we divide 75 by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the right.
Careful here. 0.75 kilometres would be 750 metres. Our 75 metres is much less, so a 0 must come after the point: 0.075.
Now join it to the 4 whole kilometres. 4 plus 0.075 is 4.075.
See it in the place chart. The 4 is in the ones, and the 7 and the 5 sit in the hundredths and thousandths.

spec.note: 4 whole kilometres, and 75 m in the thousandths

beats.say: So the track is 4.075 kilometres long.
Remember: metres to kilometres means 3 decimal places. Fill the empty place with a 0.
Meera's bottle holds 1.2 litres. She drinks 350 millilitres. How many millilitres are left?
Can we take 350 away from 1.2 just like that?

choices: no, change litres to ml first
ask.ifNot: The two amounts are in different units. We must make them both millilitres before we subtract.

beats.say: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So 1.2 litres is 1.2 times 1000, which is 1200 millilitres.
Careful: it is 1200, not 1020. The 0.2 of a litre is 200 millilitres.
She drank the water, so we take it away. 1200 minus 350.
Take away 300 first, which leaves 900. Then take away 50 more. That leaves 850.
So 850 millilitres of water are left.
Check: 850 plus 350 is 1200. It works. Same units first, then subtract.
A new pencil is 14 centimetres 6 millimetres long. After sharpening, it is 12 centimetres 9 millimetres. How many millimetres shorter is it?
The answer is wanted in millimetres. What is a good first step?

ask.ifNot: Mixed units are slippery. Let's write each length in millimetres only, then subtract once.

beats.say: 1 centimetre is 10 millimetres. So 14 centimetres is 140 millimetres, and 6 more makes 146.
The same for the short pencil. 12 centimetres is 120 millimetres, and 9 more makes 129.
Now find the gap between 129 and 146. Count up: 1 more gets us to 130, and 16 more gets us to 146.
1 and 16 make 17. So the pencil is 17 millimetres shorter.
Here is the trap to dodge. Taking 6 from 9 mixes up the two pencils: the 9 millimetres belong to the shorter one.
So change everything into the small unit first. Then it is one clean subtraction.
Amma buys 1 kilogram 750 grams of potatoes and 2 kilograms 400 grams of onions. What is the total, in kilograms?
Add the grams first. 750 plus 400 is 1150 grams.
1150 grams is more than 1000 grams. So what is hiding inside it?

choices: nothing, leave it as it is
ask.ifNot: 1000 grams make 1 kilogram. 1150 is more than 1000, so 1 whole kilogram is inside, with some grams left over.

beats.say: 1150 grams is 1 kilogram and 150 grams. That extra kilogram joins the others.
Now the kilograms. 1 plus 2, plus the 1 we carried, makes 4. So the total is 4 kilograms 150 grams.
Last step: write it as a decimal. 150 grams is 150 divided by 1000, which is 0.15 kilograms.
So the vegetables weigh 4.15 kilograms. Watch the place: 0.015 would be only 15 grams.
Remember: when the grams pass 1000, carry a kilogram across.
A fruit seller has 7 dozen bananas. He sells 3 score. How many bananas are left?
Dozen and score are names for numbers. A dozen is 12. So 7 dozen is 7 times 12, which is 84 bananas.
Now the score. How many is 1 score?

ask.ifNot: A score is 20. It is bigger than a dozen.

beats.say: A score is 20. So 3 score is 3 times 20, which is 60 bananas.
He sold 60, so we take them away. 84 minus 60 is 24.
So 24 bananas are left.
Turn the number words into numbers first. After that it is a sum you already know how to do.
A box holds 1 gross of pencils. A teacher gives 2 pencils to each of 54 children. How many pencils remain?
How many is a gross?

ask.ifNot: A gross is 12 dozen. And 12 times 12 is 144.

beats.say: A gross is 12 dozen, and 12 times 12 is 144. So the box starts with 144 pencils.
Each of the 54 children gets 2 pencils. 54 times 2 is 108.
Careful: it is 2 pencils each, not 1. If we forgot that, we would take away only 54.
Now subtract. 144 minus 108. Take away 100 to get 44, then 8 more to get 36.
So 36 pencils remain in the box.
Check: 108 given out, plus 36 left, makes 144. It fits.
A milkman pours 750 millilitres of milk into each of 6 packets. How many litres does he use?
First the total in millilitres. 6 times 700 is 4200, and 6 times 50 is 300. Together, 4500 millilitres.
The question asks for litres. How do we change millilitres into litres?

ask.ifNot: 1000 millilitres make 1 litre. Litres are bigger, so there are fewer of them. We divide by 1000.

beats.say: 1000 millilitres make 1 litre. 4500 divided by 1000 is 4.5.
So the milkman uses 4.5 litres of milk. That is 4 and a half litres.
Does it make sense? Each packet is less than 1 litre, so 6 packets must be less than 6 litres. 4.5 fits nicely.
The plan: multiply first, then change the unit at the end.
Ravi's school is 850 metres from home. He walks there and back on each of 5 school days. How many kilometres is that in the week?

board.text: 850 m to school, there and back, 5 days
How many km in the week?

beats.say: Read it slowly: there and back. How many times does Ravi walk the 850 metres in one day?

ask.ifNot: He walks to school, and then he walks home again. That is the 850 metres twice each day.

beats.say: So in one day he walks 850 times 2, which is 1700 metres.
There are 5 school days, so we need 1700 times 5. 1000 times 5 is 5000, and 700 times 5 is 3500. Together, 8500 metres.
Now change metres into kilometres. 1000 metres make 1 kilometre, so we divide by 1000.
So Ravi walks 8.5 kilometres in the week.
The trap was the walk home. Forget it and you get only half the distance. Always ask: one way, or both ways?
A carpenter cuts a plank 3 metres long into 8 equal pieces. How long is each piece, in centimetres?
The answer is wanted in centimetres. What shall we do first?

ask.ifNot: Cutting into equal pieces is sharing, so we will divide. But first, let's turn the 3 metres into centimetres.

beats.say: 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so 3 metres is 300 centimetres.
Now share 300 among 8 pieces. Halving 3 times is the same as dividing by 8. Half of 300 is 150.
Half of 150 is 75. And half of 75 is 37.5.
So each piece is 37.5 centimetres long.
Check: 8 pieces of 37.5 centimetres make 300 centimetres. And each piece is much shorter than the plank, as it should be.
A stack of 40 equal coins is 6 centimetres tall. How thick is one coin, in millimetres?
The answer is in millimetres, so change the height first. 1 centimetre is 10 millimetres, so 6 centimetres is 60 millimetres.
The 40 coins share that height equally. So which sum gives one coin?

ask.ifNot: The whole stack is 60 millimetres, shared among 40 coins. Sharing means dividing the height by the number of coins.

beats.say: 60 divided by 40. Take a zero off both, and it is 6 divided by 4. 4 goes into 6 once, with 2 left over, and 2 out of 4 is a half.
So one coin is 1.5 millimetres thick.
Check: 40 coins at 1.5 millimetres each make 60 millimetres, which is our 6 centimetres.
Change the unit first, then share. And ask if the answer is sensible: a coin really is about that thin.
Which of these 4 lengths is the greatest? They are written in different ways, so we cannot tell just by looking.

board.text: Greatest: 1.08 km, 1 km 800 m, 1008 m, 10800 cm?

beats.say: What is the fair way to compare them?

ask.ifNot: A big number with a tiny unit can still be a short length. Let's write every length in metres, then compare.

beats.say: First, 1.08 kilometres. 1 kilometre is 1000 metres, so 1.08 times 1000 is 1080 metres.
Next, 1 kilometre 800 metres. That is 1000 plus 800, which is 1800 metres.
1008 metres is already in metres. Now the last one: 10800 centimetres. 100 centimetres make 1 metre, so divide by 100. Only 108 metres!
So in metres we have 1080, 1800, 1008 and 108. Which is the biggest?

ask.ifNot: Look at the hundreds. 1800 has 8 hundreds after its thousand, more than any of the others.

beats.say: 1800 metres is the greatest. That is 1 kilometre 800 metres.
Did you see the trap? 10800 looked huge, but centimetres are tiny. Always compare in the same unit.
One tablet has 250 milligrams of medicine. How many grams are there in a strip of 10 tablets?
First the total in milligrams. 10 times 250 is 2500 milligrams.
Now we need grams. How many milligrams make 1 gram?

ask.ifNot: Milli means a thousandth. So 1000 milligrams make 1 gram.

beats.say: 1000 milligrams make 1 gram, so we divide by 1000. 2500 divided by 1000 is 2.5.
So the strip contains 2.5 grams of medicine.
Careful with the choices. 2500 is the number of milligrams, not grams. And 0.25 grams is just 1 tablet.
Multiply first, then change the unit. And always check which unit the question wants.
A tailor has 5 metres of cloth. He uses 2 metres 35 centimetres for a kurta. How much cloth is left?
Let's write both lengths in centimetres. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so 5 metres is 500 centimetres.
And 2 metres 35 centimetres is 200 plus 35, which is 235 centimetres.
Now subtract. 500 minus 200 is 300, and 300 minus 35 is 265.
265 centimetres. How do we write that in metres and centimetres?

ask.ifNot: Every 100 centimetres is 1 metre. 265 has 2 hundreds, with 65 left over.

beats.say: 265 is 200 and 65. So 2 metres 65 centimetres of cloth is left.
The trap is 3 metres 65. To take away the 35 centimetres, one of the metres had to be broken into 100 centimetres.
Check: 235 used, plus 265 left, makes 500. It works.
A running track is 4 hectometres long. Sunil runs 5 rounds. How many kilometres does he run?
What does hecto mean?

ask.ifNot: Hecto means a hundred. So a hectometre is a hundred metres.

beats.say: 1 hectometre is 100 metres. So one round is 4 times 100, which is 400 metres.
Sunil runs 5 rounds. 400 times 5 is 2000 metres.
Now change to kilometres. 1000 metres make 1 kilometre, and 2000 divided by 1000 is 2.
So Sunil runs 2 kilometres.
Remember: hecto is a hundred, and kilo is a thousand. Change to metres first, and the rest is easy.
Rina needs 150 laddoos. The shop sells them only in boxes of one dozen. What is the least number of boxes she must buy?

board.text: 150 laddoos. Boxes of 1 dozen. Fewest boxes?

beats.say: A dozen is 12. So we ask: how many 12s do we need to reach 150? Start with 10 boxes: 12 times 10 is 120.
2 more boxes give 24 more laddoos. 120 plus 24 is 144. So 12 boxes hold 144 laddoos.
Rina needs 150, and 12 boxes give 144. Is that enough?

ask.ifNot: 150 minus 144 is 6. She would be 6 laddoos short, and her guests would notice!

beats.say: She cannot buy part of a box. So she needs one whole box more. 12 plus 1 is 13 boxes.
13 boxes hold 156 laddoos, which is enough. So Rina must buy 13 boxes.
When things come in packs, a remainder means one more pack. Round up, so that there is enough.
Arjun walks 2 kilometres 75 metres, then 850 metres, then 1.5 kilometres. How many kilometres in all?
The 3 distances are written in 3 different ways. What is the safest plan?

choices: change all to metres, then add
ask.ifNot: Different units cannot be added as they are. Let's put all of them in metres, add, and change back at the end.

beats.say: 1 kilometre is 1000 metres. So 2 kilometres 75 metres is 2000 plus 75, which is 2075 metres.
Careful: 2075, not 2750. The 75 metres are just 75.
850 metres is already in metres. And 1.5 kilometres is 1.5 times 1000, which is 1500 metres.
Now add. 2075 plus 1500 is 3575. Then 850 more makes 4425 metres.
Back to kilometres: divide by 1000. 4425 divided by 1000 is 4.425.
So Arjun walks 4.425 kilometres in all.
The plan: everything into the small unit, add, then change back.
An empty basket weighs 600 grams. With 12 equal mangoes in it, it weighs 4 kilograms 200 grams. What does one mango weigh?

board.text: Basket 600 g. Basket + 12 mangoes = 4 kg 200 g.

beats.say: First make it all grams. 4 kilograms is 4000 grams, and 200 more makes 4200 grams.
Is 4200 grams the weight of the mangoes?

choices: no, the basket is in there too
ask.ifNot: The scale weighed the basket and the mangoes together. We must take the basket's 600 grams away first.

beats.say: Take the basket away. 4200 minus 600 is 3600 grams. That is the 12 mangoes alone.
Now share 3600 among 12 mangoes. 36 divided by 12 is 3, so 3600 divided by 12 is 300.
So one mango weighs 300 grams.
Check: 12 mangoes weigh 3600 grams, and the basket's 600 makes 4200. It fits.
When something is weighed in a container, take the container away first.
A leaking tap drips 5 millilitres of water every minute. How many litres does it waste in one full day?
Let's climb in steps: a minute, then an hour, then a day. An hour has 60 minutes, and a day has 24 hours.
So how much water drips away in one hour?

ask.ifNot: The tap loses 5 millilitres in every one of the 60 minutes. So we multiply 5 by 60.

beats.say: 5 times 60 is 300. The tap wastes 300 millilitres every hour.
Now a whole day: 300 times 24. 3 times 24 is 72, so 300 times 24 is 7200 millilitres.
Change to litres. 1000 millilitres make 1 litre, so 7200 divided by 1000 is 7.2.
So the tap wastes 7.2 litres in a day. That is more than 7 big bottles of water, from tiny drips!
The trap is to stop at 300, which is only one hour. Go up step by step and you will not miss one.
A snail crawls 3 centimetres 5 millimetres every minute. How many minutes does it take to crawl 2.1 metres?

board.text: 3 cm 5 mm each minute. 2.1 m takes ? minutes

beats.say: Centimetres, millimetres and metres are all mixed up here. Which single unit shall we use for everything?

ask.ifNot: The smallest unit here is the millimetre. If we use it for everything, there are no decimals to worry about.

beats.say: 1 centimetre is 10 millimetres. So 3 centimetres is 30 millimetres, and 5 more makes 35 millimetres each minute.
Now the 2.1 metres. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, and each of those is 10 millimetres. So 1 metre is 1000 millimetres.
2.1 times 1000 is 2100 millimetres. Careful, not 210: that would be the centimetres.
So the snail must go 2100 millimetres, at 35 each minute. How many 35s are in 2100? 35 times 2 is 70, and 70 times 30 is 2100.
2 times 30 is 60. So 35 times 60 is 2100, and the snail takes 60 minutes.
That is exactly one hour. The plan: one unit for everything, then divide the distance by the distance each minute.
Pencils come in packets of a dozen, and erasers in packets of a score. Asha wants exactly as many pencils as erasers. What is the smallest number of pencils she can buy?

board.text: Pencils in dozens, erasers in scores.
Same number of each. Smallest number?

beats.say: A dozen is 12 and a score is 20. So the pencils must be a number in the 12 times table, and the erasers a number in the 20 times table.
The two numbers must be equal. So what kind of number are we hunting for?

ask.ifNot: The pencils are in the 12 times table and the erasers are in the 20 times table. They are equal, so the number is in both tables.

beats.say: Let's list the 20s, because they grow faster: 20, 40, 60. Now test each one. Does 12 go into it exactly?
12 does not go into 20. And 12 times 3 is 36, 12 times 4 is 48, so it jumps right over 40 too.
But 12 times 5 is 60. So 60 is in both tables: 5 packets of pencils and 3 packets of erasers.
So the smallest number of pencils Asha can buy is 60.
The trap is 12 times 20, which is 240. That works, but it is not the smallest. List the multiples and take the first match.
A straight fence is 20 metres long. There is a post at each end, and the posts are 2 metres 50 centimetres apart. How many posts are there?

board.text: Fence 20 m. Posts every 2 m 50 cm, one at each end.

beats.say: Make the units match. 20 metres is 2000 centimetres, and 2 metres 50 centimetres is 250 centimetres.
How many gaps of 250 fit in 2000? 4 gaps make 1000, so 8 gaps make 2000.
So there are 8 gaps. Is the number of posts also 8?

spec.note: Count the gaps between the marks

ask.ifNot: Look at the line. Every gap has a post at its far end, and there is one extra post right at the start.

beats.say: Think of your hand: 5 fingers, but only 4 gaps between them. Posts in a straight line are always one more than the gaps.
8 gaps, plus 1, makes 9 posts.
Remember: with a post at both ends, count the gaps, then add 1.
Amma pours 1 litre 200 millilitres of juice equally into 8 glasses. The children drink 3 glasses. How many litres are left?
First, all in millilitres. 1 litre is 1000 millilitres, and 200 more makes 1200.
Share 1200 among 8 glasses by halving 3 times: 600, then 300, then 150. So each glass holds 150 millilitres.
The children drink 3 glasses. The question asks what is left. How many glasses still have juice?

ask.ifNot: There were 8 glasses and 3 were drunk. 8 take away 3 leaves 5 full glasses.

beats.say: 5 glasses are left, each with 150 millilitres. 5 times 150 is 750 millilitres.
The answer must be in litres. 750 divided by 1000 is 0.75.
So 0.75 litres of juice are left.
Two traps here. 3 glasses is what was drunk, not what is left. And the last step is to change into litres.
Each step Anu takes is 60 centimetres long. How many steps does she take to walk 1.5 kilometres?
Her steps are in centimetres, but the walk is in kilometres. What comes first?

ask.ifNot: We can only count how many steps fit when both lengths are in the same unit. Let's change the kilometres into centimetres.

beats.say: Go down one unit at a time. 1 kilometre is 1000 metres, so 1.5 kilometres is 1500 metres.
Each metre is 100 centimetres. 1500 times 100 is 150000 centimetres. Count the zeros carefully!
Now, how many 60s are in 150000? Take one zero off both numbers: it is 15000 divided by 6.
15 divided by 6 is 2.5. So 15000 divided by 6 is 2500.
So Anu takes 2500 steps.
Check: 2500 steps of 60 centimetres make 150000 centimetres. It fits. Most slips here are lost zeros, so count them.
A shopkeeper buys 1 gross of pens for 720 rupees and sells them at 8 rupees each. How much does he gain on one score of pens?

board.text: Buys 1 gross for ₹720. Sells at ₹8 each.

beats.say: A gross is 12 dozen. 12 times 12 is 144, so that is 144 pens. And a score is 20 pens.
First, what did one pen cost him? 144 times 5 is 720. So each pen cost 5 rupees.
He buys a pen for 5 rupees and sells it for 8 rupees. What is his gain on one pen?

ask.ifNot: Gain is what he gets, minus what he paid. 8 take away 5.

beats.say: 8 minus 5 is 3. He gains 3 rupees on every pen.
A score is 20 pens. 20 times 3 is 60.
So he gains 60 rupees on one score of pens.
Careful with the choices. 160 is what he sells 20 pens for, and 100 is what he paid for them. The gain is the gap between those.
A frog is at the bottom of a well 2 metres 60 centimetres deep. Each day it climbs 50 centimetres, and each night it slips back 20. On which day does it climb out?

board.text: Well: 2 m 60 cm. Up 50 cm by day, down 20 cm at night.

beats.say: The well is 200 plus 60, which is 260 centimetres deep. In one full day and night the frog goes up 50 and down 20, so it gains 30.
Many people now divide 260 by 30 and say about 9 days. But think: what happens on the frog's last day?

choices: it gets out before it can slip
ask.ifNot: Once the frog reaches the top in the daytime, it is out. It does not slip back that night.

beats.say: So the last climb is a full 50 centimetres. The frog only needs to be 210 centimetres up before that last day.
How many full days and nights does it take to reach 210? The frog gains 30 each time, and 7 times 30 is 210.
After 7 days and nights it is at 210. On the next day it climbs 50 and reaches 260. It is out!
The day after day 7 is day 8. So the frog climbs out on the 8th day.
In slip-back puzzles, treat the last climb on its own. That is the whole secret.
Three parcels weigh 2.4 kilograms, 2 kilograms 50 grams, and 2450 grams. The lightest and the heaviest go on a scale together. What does it show?
To see which is lightest and which is heaviest, put all 3 in grams. 2.4 kilograms is 2.4 times 1000, which is 2400 grams.
Now 2 kilograms 50 grams. How many grams is that?

ask.ifNot: 2 kilograms is 2 thousand grams. Then add just 50 more.

beats.say: 2000 plus 50 is 2050 grams. Careful: not 2500. 50 grams is a small amount.
So the parcels are 2400, 2050 and 2450 grams. The lightest is 2050 and the heaviest is 2450.
Add those two. 2050 plus 2450 is 4500 grams.
4500 divided by 1000 is 4.5. So the scale shows 4.5 kilograms.
The surprise was that 2 kilograms 50 grams is the lightest. Put everything in one unit before you compare.
A plumber cuts a pipe 12 metres long into pieces of 1 metre 50 centimetres. Each cut takes 4 minutes. How long does all the cutting take?

board.text: Pipe 12 m. Pieces of 1 m 50 cm. 4 minutes a cut.

beats.say: First, how many pieces? In centimetres the pipe is 1200 and each piece is 150.
2 pieces make 300 centimetres, which is 3 metres. So 12 metres gives 4 lots of 2 pieces. That is 8 pieces.
8 pieces. So how many cuts does the plumber make?

ask.ifNot: Try it with a strip of paper. One cut makes 2 pieces. Two cuts make 3 pieces. The cuts are always one fewer than the pieces.

beats.say: Each cut is a place where two pieces meet. 8 pieces in a row meet at 7 places. So there are 7 cuts.
Each cut takes 4 minutes. 7 times 4 is 28.
So all the cutting takes 28 minutes.
The trap is 8 times 4, which is 32. Pieces are not cuts: the cuts are one fewer.
6 strips of paper, each 25 centimetres long, are glued end to end. At every join they overlap by 15 millimetres. How long is the finished strip?

board.text: 6 strips of 25 cm. Each join overlaps 15 mm.

beats.say: With no overlap at all, the strip would be 6 times 25, which is 150 centimetres.
But each join hides a little paper. 6 strips in a row: how many joins?

ask.ifNot: Joins sit between the strips. 2 strips have 1 join, and 3 strips have 2 joins. There is always one fewer join than strips.

beats.say: 6 strips have 5 joins.
Each overlap is 15 millimetres. 10 millimetres make 1 centimetre, so that is 1.5 centimetres. Careful: not 15 centimetres!
5 joins, each hiding 1.5 centimetres. 5 times 1.5 is 7.5 centimetres lost.
Take that away from 150. 150 minus 7.5 is 142.5. So the finished strip is 142.5 centimetres long.
Two things to watch: count the joins, not the strips, and make the units match.
An empty tank holds 50 litres. A tap pours in 4 litres every minute. After 5 minutes a drain opens too, and lets out 1 litre 500 millilitres every minute. When is the tank full?

board.text: Tank 50 litres. Tap: 4 litres a minute.
After 5 minutes, drain: 1 litre 500 ml a minute.

beats.say: This story has two parts. First part: 5 minutes with only the tap. 5 times 4 is 20 litres in the tank.
So how much more is needed? 50 minus 20 is 30 litres.
Second part: the tap puts in 4 litres a minute, but the drain takes out 1 and a half. How fast does the water rise now?

ask.ifNot: Water comes in and water goes out, so we subtract. 4 take away 1 and a half.

beats.say: 1 litre 500 millilitres is 1.5 litres. 4 minus 1.5 is 2.5. The water now rises 2.5 litres each minute.
2.5 litres a minute means 5 litres every 2 minutes. We need 30 litres, which is 6 lots of 5. So 6 times 2 is 12 minutes.
Careful: 12 minutes is only the second part. Add the first 5 minutes. 5 plus 12 is 17.
So the tank is full 17 minutes after the tap was turned on.
When a story changes halfway, solve each part on its own, then add the times.
A baker needs 14 dozen eggs. Eggs come only in trays of 30. He buys the fewest trays that give enough. How many eggs are left over?
A dozen is 12. 14 times 10 is 140, and 14 times 2 is 28. So he needs 168 eggs.
Now count the trays in 30s. 5 trays give 150 eggs.
He needs 168. Are 5 trays enough?

ask.ifNot: 150 is less than 168, so some eggs would be missing. He must buy one more tray.

beats.say: 6 trays give 180 eggs. That is enough.
He uses 168 of them. 180 minus 168 is 12.
So 12 eggs are left over. That is exactly 1 dozen!
Read the last line of a question twice. It asked for the eggs left over, not the number of trays.
4 shops sell the same milk. P sells 500 millilitres for 28 rupees. Q sells 1.5 litres for 81. R sells 250 millilitres for 15. S sells 2 litres for 110.
The sizes are all different. What is the fair way to compare the shops?

choices: find the price of 1 litre at each
ask.ifNot: A small price for a tiny bottle is not a bargain. We need the price of the same amount, 1 litre, at every shop.

beats.say: Shop P: 500 millilitres is half a litre. So a litre costs 2 times 28, which is 56 rupees.
Shop R: 250 millilitres is a quarter of a litre. So a litre costs 4 times 15, which is 60 rupees. The smallest price tag, but the dearest milk!
Shop S: 2 litres cost 110, so 1 litre is half of that. 55 rupees.
Shop Q is the tricky one. 1.5 litres is 3 half litres. 81 divided by 3 is 27 for each half litre, so a litre costs 54 rupees.
Now compare: 56, 60, 55 and 54. The least is 54, at Shop Q.
To compare prices, work out the cost of the same amount at each shop. Then the best deal is easy to spot.
A box with 12 equal tins weighs 5 kilograms 100 grams. With 4 tins taken out, it weighs 3 kilograms 500 grams. What does the empty box weigh?
Let's work in grams. The first weighing is 5100 grams and the second is 3500 grams.
The weight dropped when 4 tins came out. So what does the drop tell us?

ask.ifNot: The box stayed. Only 4 tins left. So the weight that vanished is exactly the weight of those 4 tins.

beats.say: 5100 minus 3500 is 1600. So 4 tins weigh 1600 grams.
One tin is 1600 divided by 4, which is 400 grams.
All 12 tins weigh 12 times 400, which is 4800 grams.
The full box was 5100 grams. Take the tins away: 5100 minus 4800 is 300.
So the empty box weighs 300 grams.
Careful: 400 grams is one tin, not the box. Keep going until you have answered what was asked.
A book's pages are numbered 1 to 300. Each sheet carries 2 pages and is 0.1 millimetres thick. There are 2 covers, each 2 millimetres thick. How thick is the book?

board.text: Pages 1 to 300. A sheet = 2 pages, 0.1 mm thick.

beats.say: Each sheet has a page on the front and a page on the back. So how many sheets make 300 pages?

ask.ifNot: Pick up one sheet of any book: it has 2 page numbers. So the sheets are half the pages.

beats.say: 300 divided by 2 is 150 sheets.
Each sheet is 0.1 millimetres, which is one tenth. So 10 sheets make 1 millimetre, and 150 sheets make 15 millimetres.
Now the covers. There are 2, each 2 millimetres thick. That adds 4 millimetres.
15 plus 4 is 19 millimetres.
The choices are in centimetres. 10 millimetres make 1 centimetre, so 19 divided by 10 is 1.9.
So the book is 1.9 centimetres thick.
Three traps in one question: sheets are not pages, there are two covers, and the unit changes at the end.
Rani needs 3 metres of lace. She has pieces of 1 metre 20 centimetres, 85 centimetres and 600 millimetres. How many more centimetres does she need?

board.text: Needs 3 m. Has 1 m 20 cm, 85 cm, 600 mm.

beats.say: Put every piece in centimetres. 1 metre 20 centimetres is 100 plus 20, which is 120. The 85 is already in centimetres.
And 600 millimetres? Remember, 10 millimetres make 1 centimetre.

ask.ifNot: Divide by 10. For 600 divided by 10, just take one zero off.

beats.say: 600 divided by 10 is 60 centimetres.
Add the 3 pieces. 120 plus 85 is 205, and 60 more makes 265 centimetres.
She needs 3 metres, which is 300 centimetres. 300 minus 265 is 35.
So Rani needs 35 centimetres more lace.
Careful: 265 is what she has, not what she still needs. Always finish the question.
We need to change 3 metres into centimetres.
Which is the smaller unit: a metre or a centimetre?

ask.ifNot: A centimetre is about the width of your fingernail. A metre is one big step. So the centimetre is much smaller.

beats.say: Small units mean we need more of them. 1 metre is 100 centimetres. A metre ruler has 100 little centimetres marked on it.
We have 3 metres, so that is 3 lots of 100. 3 times 100 is 300.
So 3 metres is 300 centimetres.
Metres to centimetres: multiply by 100. That means two zeros go on the end.
A bag of rice weighs 5 kilograms. How many grams is that?
Grams are small. A paper clip weighs about 1 gram! So a bag of rice will be a lot of grams.
How many grams make 1 kilogram?

ask.ifNot: Kilo means a thousand. So 1 kilogram is 1000 grams.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. We have 5 kilograms, so we need 5 lots of 1000.
5 times 1000 is 5000.
So the bag weighs 5000 grams.
Kilograms to grams: multiply by 1000. Three zeros go on the end.
A jug holds 2000 millilitres of water. How many litres is that?
A millilitre is tiny, just a few drops. A litre is a big bottle. So we will get far fewer litres than millilitres.
How many millilitres make 1 litre?

ask.ifNot: Milli means a thousandth. So it takes 1000 millilitres to fill 1 litre.

beats.say: 1000 millilitres make 1 litre. So we ask: how many 1000s are in 2000?
1000 and another 1000 make 2000. That is 2 lots.
So the jug holds 2 litres.
Millilitres to litres: divide by 1000.
How many eggs are there in 2 dozen?
Dozen is a special word for a number. Which number?

ask.ifNot: A dozen is 12. Eggs are often sold in boxes of 12, a dozen eggs.

beats.say: 1 dozen is 12. So 2 dozen is 2 lots of 12.
12 plus 12 is 24. Or, 2 times 12 is 24.
So there are 24 eggs in 2 dozen.
Remember: a dozen is always 12.
Amma buys half a dozen bananas. How many bananas is that?
First, how many is a whole dozen?

ask.ifNot: A dozen is 12. Think of a box of 12 eggs.

beats.say: A dozen is 12. Half means we split it into 2 equal parts and take one part.
12 divided by 2 is 6, because 6 and 6 make 12.
So Amma buys 6 bananas.
Half a dozen is 6. You will hear that in shops all the time.
Riya buys 250 grams of sugar and 500 grams of flour. What is the total weight?
Total means all of it together. So do we add or subtract?

ask.ifNot: Total means putting both together. So we add the two weights.

beats.say: Both weights are in grams, so we can add them straight away.
Add the hundreds first. 200 plus 500 is 700.
Then the 50 that was left over. 700 plus 50 is 750.
So the total weight is 750 grams.
When the units are the same, just add the numbers and keep the unit.
A rope is 8 metres long. Ravi cuts off a piece 3 metres long. How long is the rope that is left?
After the cut, is the rope longer or shorter?

ask.ifNot: A piece has been cut off and taken away. So the rope that is left must be shorter.

beats.say: Shorter means we take away. We start with 8 and take away 3.
Count back 3 from 8: 7, 6, 5.
So 5 metres of rope is left.
Check: the 5 metres left and the 3 metres cut off make 8 metres again.
Which unit is best for measuring the weight of a watermelon?

board.text: Weight of a watermelon: which unit?

beats.say: Weight tells us how heavy something is. Which of these measures how heavy?

ask.ifNot: Litres are for liquids and centimetres are for lengths. Heaviness is measured in grams and kilograms.

beats.say: Let's sort the units. Litre and millilitre measure liquids, like juice.
Centimetre measures length, like how long your pencil is.
Kilogram measures weight. And a watermelon is heavy, a few kilograms, so it fits well.
So the best unit is the kilogram.
Always ask first: am I measuring a length, a weight, or a liquid?
Which of these lengths is the longest: 1 centimetre, 1 metre, 1 millimetre or 1 kilometre?

board.text: Longest: 1 cm, 1 m, 1 mm or 1 km?

beats.say: Every number is 1, so the numbers cannot help us. We have to think about the units themselves.
A millimetre is tiny, like the thickness of a coin's edge. A centimetre is about the width of your fingernail.
A metre is about one big step. What about a kilometre?

ask.ifNot: Kilo means a thousand. A kilometre is a thousand metres: a walk of many minutes.

beats.say: 1 kilometre is 1000 metres. That is far longer than all the others.
So the longest length is 1 kilometre.
From smallest to biggest: millimetre, centimetre, metre, kilometre. Keep that order in your head.
A shopkeeper has 4 bottles of juice. Each bottle holds 2 litres. How many litres does he have in all?
4 bottles, with the same amount in each. Which sum finds the total?

ask.ifNot: There are 4 equal lots of 2 litres. Equal lots mean we multiply: 4 times 2.

beats.say: We can see it by adding the bottles one by one: 2, 4, 6, 8.
That is the same as 4 times 2, which is 8.
So he has 8 litres of juice in all.
Equal groups mean multiply. Just adding 4 and 2 would not count all the bottles.
A pencil is 15 centimetres long and an eraser is 5 centimetres long. They are placed end to end. How long is the line they make?

board.text: 15 cm and 5 cm, end to end. Length?

beats.say: End to end means one starts where the other stops. So what do we do with the two lengths?

ask.ifNot: The line is as long as the pencil, and then the eraser after it. So we put the two lengths together: we add.

beats.say: The line is the pencil's 15 centimetres, and then 5 more for the eraser.
5 plus 5 is 10. So 15 plus 5 is 20.
So the line is 20 centimetres long.
End to end means add. Both lengths were in centimetres, so the answer is in centimetres too.
A fruit seller has 36 bananas. How many dozen is that?
A dozen is 12. So we are asking: how many 12s make 36?
Let's count in 12s. 12, then 24, then what?

ask.ifNot: Add 12 to 24. 24 plus 10 is 34, and 2 more makes 36.

beats.say: 12, 24, 36. We counted 3 twelves to reach 36.
So 36 bananas make 3 dozen.
Check: 3 times 12 is 36. To find how many dozen, divide by 12.
Which of the choices is the same as 11.11 kilograms? Let's turn 11.11 kilograms into kilograms and grams, then compare.
Split the number at the decimal point. 11 whole kilograms, and 0.11 of a kilogram.
The 11 kilograms are easy. But what is 0.11 kilograms in grams? Remember, 1 kilogram is 1000 grams.

ask.ifNot: Multiply 0.11 by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the left, so 0.11 becomes 110.

beats.say: 0.11 times 1000 is 110. So 0.11 kilograms is 110 grams.
Here is the trap. 11 kilograms 11 grams looks just like 11.11. But 11 grams is only 0.011 kilograms.
So 11.11 kilograms is 11 kilograms 110 grams.
The method: split at the decimal point, keep the whole kilograms, and change only the decimal part into grams.
500 sheets of paper make a pile 5 centimetres thick. Mr. Deepak's big stack is 1 metre 22.5 centimetres thick. How many sheets are in it?

board.text: Stack: 1 m 22.5 cm. How many sheets?

beats.say: First, let's make the stack's thickness all centimetres. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so the stack is 100 plus 22.5. That is 122.5 centimetres.
Now, 500 sheets fill 5 centimetres. So how many sheets fit in just 1 centimetre?

ask.ifNot: Share the 500 sheets equally over the 5 centimetres. That is 500 divided by 5.

beats.say: 500 divided by 5 is 100. So every centimetre of the stack holds 100 sheets.
The stack is 122.5 centimetres thick, so we need 122.5 times 100. Times 100 slides the digits 2 places to the left.
So there were 12250 sheets in all.
Does that make sense? 100 centimetres alone would hold 10000 sheets, so a bit more than that is just right.
The plan: find how many fit in 1 centimetre, then multiply by the number of centimetres.
Here is a sum with a twist. 2 metres, plus 2 decimetres, plus 15 centimetres. Each length has its own unit.
Can we just add 2 and 2 and 15? Not yet. What must we do first?

ask.ifNot: Lengths can only be added when they are in the same unit. The choices are in centimetres, so let's change everything into centimetres.

beats.say: Start with the metres. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so 2 metres is 200 centimetres.
Now the decimetres. A decimetre is 10 centimetres, so 2 decimetres is 20 centimetres.
The 15 centimetres are already centimetres. Now everything matches, so we can add. 200 plus 20 is 220.
And 15 more makes 235. So the total is 235 centimetres.
Remember: same units first, then add. Never just push the numbers together.
We have 7 kilograms and 70 grams, and we want one decimal number in kilograms.
The 7 kilograms stay. Only the 70 grams need changing. 1000 grams make 1 kilogram, so we divide 70 by 1000.
What is 70 divided by 1000?

ask.ifNot: Dividing by 1000 slides the digits 3 places to the right. The 7 lands in the hundredths place.

beats.say: 70 divided by 1000 is 0.07. The 7 sits in the hundredths place.
Careful, this is where many people slip. 0.70 kilograms would be 700 grams, ten times too much. And 0.007 would be just 7 grams.
Now add the 7 whole kilograms. 7 plus 0.07 is 7.07.
So 7 kilograms 70 grams is 7.07 kilograms.
Remember: grams to kilograms, divide by 1000, and watch where each digit lands.
8.05 kilograms is a decimal way of writing some kilograms and some grams. Which ones?
Split it at the point. 8 whole kilograms, and 0.05 of a kilogram.
1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So to turn 0.05 kilograms into grams, we multiply by 1000.
What is 0.05 times 1000?

ask.ifNot: Times 1000 slides the digits 3 places to the left. So 0.05 becomes 50.

beats.say: 0.05 times 1000 is 50. So 0.05 kilograms is 50 grams.
Watch the 0 after the point. 0.5 kilograms would be 500 grams, but we have 0.05, which is ten times smaller.
So 8.05 kilograms is 8 kilograms 50 grams.
The method: split at the point, keep the whole kilograms, and change the decimal part into grams.
Twelve dozen notebooks are piled up, and each one is 5 millimetres thick. How high is the pile?

board.text: 12 dozen notebooks, each 5 mm thick. Height?

beats.say: First, how many notebooks is twelve dozen? A dozen is 12.

ask.ifNot: Twelve dozen means 12 lots of 12. That is 12 times 12.

beats.say: 12 times 12 is 144. So there are 144 notebooks.
Each is 5 millimetres thick, so we need 144 times 5. A trick: 144 times 10 is 1440, and 5 is half of 10, so halve it. 720 millimetres.
Now look at the choices. 720 millimetres is not there, but one choice is in centimetres. 10 millimetres make 1 centimetre.
720 divided by 10 is 72. So the pile is 72 centimetres high.
So do not rush to 'none of these'. Sometimes the answer is hiding in a different unit.
Each bean weighs 2.5 grams, and all the beans in the bag weigh half a kilogram. How many beans are there?

board.text: Bean: 2.5 g. Bag: half a kg. How many beans?

beats.say: One weight is in grams and the other is in kilograms. What do we do first?

ask.ifNot: We can only compare weights that are in the same unit. Let's change the bag's weight into grams.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams, and half of 1000 is 500. So the beans weigh 500 grams.
Now, 2.5 is an awkward number to divide by. Here is a trick: take 2 beans together. 2.5 plus 2.5 is 5 grams.
So every pair of beans weighs 5 grams. How many 5s are there in 500?

ask.ifNot: 5 goes into 5 once. So into 500 it goes 100 times.

beats.say: 500 divided by 5 is 100. That is 100 pairs of beans.
Careful: 100 is the number of pairs, not beans. Each pair is 2 beans, so we double it. 200 beans.
Check: 200 beans at 2.5 grams each is 500 grams. It fits. Same units first, then count how many fit.
7 kilograms 70 grams. Let's write that weight as a single decimal number of kilograms.
The 7 kilograms stay. Only the 70 grams need changing. 1000 grams make 1 kilogram, so we divide 70 by 1000.
What is 70 divided by 1000?

ask.ifNot: Dividing by 1000 slides the digits 3 places to the right. The 7 lands in the hundredths place.

beats.say: 70 divided by 1000 is 0.07. The 7 sits in the hundredths place.
Careful, this is where many people slip. 0.70 kilograms would be 700 grams, ten times too much. And 0.007 would be just 7 grams.
Now add the 7 whole kilograms. 7 plus 0.07 is 7.07.
So 7 kilograms 70 grams is 7.07 kilograms.
So the rule is: divide the grams by 1000, then check the place of every digit before you choose.
A ribbon is 6.9 metres long. How many pieces of 3 centimetres can be cut from it?

board.text: 6.9 m ribbon. Pieces of 3 cm. How many?

beats.say: Can we just divide 6.9 by 3?

choices: no, make the units the same first
ask.ifNot: The ribbon is in metres but the pieces are in centimetres. We must change the ribbon into centimetres first.

beats.say: 1 metre is 100 centimetres. So 6.9 metres is 6.9 times 100, which is 690 centimetres.
Careful: 690, not 69. Times 100 moves the digits 2 places.
Now, how many 3s are in 690? 69 divided by 3 is 23, so 690 divided by 3 is 230.
So 230 pieces can be cut.
Check: 230 pieces of 3 centimetres make 690 centimetres. Same units first, then divide.
One bottle holds 125 millilitres of oil. How many bottles do we need for 2.5 litres?

board.text: Bottle: 125 ml. Oil: 2.5 litres. How many bottles?

beats.say: First, the same unit. 1 litre is 1000 millilitres, so 2.5 litres is 2500 millilitres.
Think about 1 litre first. 2 bottles hold 250 millilitres. So how many bottles fill 1000?

ask.ifNot: 4 lots of 250 make 1000. Each 250 is 2 bottles, so that is 8 bottles.

beats.say: 8 bottles fill 1 litre.
We have 2 and a half litres. 2 litres need 16 bottles, and the half litre needs 4 more.
16 plus 4 is 20. So 20 bottles are needed.
Check: 20 bottles of 125 millilitres make 2500 millilitres. It fits.
Someone wants to measure the perimeter of a classroom. Which of these units should they use?

board.text: Perimeter of a classroom: which unit?

beats.say: The perimeter is the distance all the way round the walls. Imagine walking round the room with your hand on the wall.

board.text: perimeter = distance all the way round

beats.say: So what kind of thing is a perimeter?

ask.ifNot: A perimeter tells us how far it is around the room. How far is a length.

beats.say: Now check each unit. Litres measure liquids, like milk. Kilograms measure how heavy something is.
Metres measure length. And a classroom is a few metres long, so the metre is just the right size.
What about 'any of these'? Each unit measures one kind of thing only, so that cannot be right. The answer is the metre.
Before you measure anything, ask yourself: is it a length, a weight, or a liquid? Then choose the unit.
How do we change decametres into decimetres? The two words look alike, so let's go slowly.

board.text: decametre → decimetre: what do we do?

beats.say: Deca means ten. So 1 decametre is 10 metres. Deci means a tenth. So 1 metre is 10 decimetres.
Which one is the smaller unit?

ask.ifNot: A decimetre is only a tenth of a metre, about the length of a crayon. A decametre is 10 whole metres.

beats.say: We are going from a big unit to a small one. So there will be more of them, and that means we multiply.
Two steps down: decametre to metre is times 10, and metre to decimetre is times 10 again. 10 times 10 is 100.
So to change decametres into decimetres, we multiply by 100.
Going to a smaller unit: multiply. Going to a bigger unit: divide. And count the steps between them.
We want a pair of units where one is 1 hundredth of the other.

board.text: Which pair: one unit = 1/100 of the other?

beats.say: Let's test each pair. A kilogram and a tonne: 1000 kilograms make a tonne. That is a thousandth, not a hundredth.
A metre and a kilometre: 1000 metres make a kilometre. A thousandth again.
A gram and a decagram: deca means ten, so 10 grams make a decagram. That is a tenth.
That leaves centilitre and litre. What does centi mean?

ask.ifNot: Think of a century, which is 100 years, or a centimetre: 100 of them make a metre. Centi means a hundredth.

beats.say: 100 centilitres make 1 litre. So a centilitre is 1 hundredth of a litre. That is our pair.
The start of the word tells you: deci is a tenth, centi is a hundredth, milli is a thousandth.
125 millilitres is what part of a litre? The answer will be a fraction.
1000 millilitres make 1 litre. So 125 millilitres is 125 out of 1000.
That fraction is clumsy, so let's make it simpler. 125 doubled is 250. 250 doubled is 500. And 500 doubled is 1000.
We doubled 3 times. So how many 125s make 1000?

ask.ifNot: Doubling 3 times is 2 times 2 times 2. That makes 8.

beats.say: 8 times 125 is 1000. So we can divide the top and the bottom of the fraction by 125.
125 millilitres is 1 eighth of a litre.
So 8 small glasses of 125 millilitres fill 1 litre. Write the part over the whole, then simplify.
37.02 kilograms. Let's write it as kilograms and grams.
Split it at the point. 37 whole kilograms, and 0.02 of a kilogram.
1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So what is 0.02 kilograms in grams?

ask.ifNot: Multiply 0.02 by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the left, so 0.02 becomes 20.

beats.say: 0.02 times 1000 is 20. So 0.02 kilograms is 20 grams.
Careful: it is not 2 grams. 2 grams would be 0.002 kilograms, with one more 0.
So 37.02 kilograms is 37 kilograms 20 grams.
Split at the point, keep the whole kilograms, and multiply the decimal part by 1000.
How many articles make 0.3 score? An article just means one thing, one item.
First, how many is 1 whole score?

ask.ifNot: A score is 20. A dozen is 12.

beats.say: 1 score is 20. So 0.3 score is 0.3 times 20.
0.3 means 3 tenths. One tenth of 20 is 2.
So 3 tenths of 20 is 3 times 2, which is 6.
So 0.3 score is 6 articles.
0.3 score is less than 1 score, so the answer must be less than 20. Always check the size of your answer.
How many gross make a dozen? That sounds upside down, so let's think carefully.
A gross is 12 dozen. That is 12 times 12, which is 144 things.
Which is bigger: a gross or a dozen?

ask.ifNot: A gross holds 12 dozens inside it. So a gross is much bigger than a dozen.

beats.say: A dozen is smaller than a gross. So a dozen is only a part of a gross. The answer must be a fraction, less than 1.
12 dozens make 1 gross. So 1 dozen is 1 of 12 equal parts of a gross. That is 1 twelfth.
So 1 twelfth of a gross makes a dozen.
Careful with the choices. 12 is how many dozens make a gross, and 144 is how many things. The question asked it the other way round.
We must add 4 kilometres, 40 metres and 400 centimetres, and give the answer in metres.
Three different units. What do we do before adding?

ask.ifNot: We can only add lengths in the same unit. The answer is wanted in metres, so let's change each part into metres.

beats.say: 1 kilometre is 1000 metres. So 4 kilometres is 4000 metres.
The 40 metres are already in metres. They stay as 40.
Now the centimetres. 100 centimetres make 1 metre, so 400 centimetres is 400 divided by 100. Only 4 metres.
Careful there: going to a bigger unit, the number gets smaller. 400 centimetres is not 400 metres.
Now add. 4000 plus 40 plus 4 is 4044.
So the total is 4044 metres.
We need to change 5 hectometres into decimetres.
Let's go through metres. Hecto means a hundred, so 1 hectometre is 100 metres. 5 hectometres is 500 metres.
Now metres to decimetres. Deci means a tenth. So how many decimetres are in 1 metre?

ask.ifNot: A decimetre is a tenth of a metre. So it takes 10 of them to make 1 whole metre.

beats.say: 1 metre is 10 decimetres. So 500 metres is 500 times 10, which is 5000 decimetres.
So 5 hectometres is 5000 decimetres.
Careful: 500 is in the choices, but that is the metres. We needed one more step down.
Times 100, then times 10. Altogether that is times 1000.
We want to write 800 grams in kilograms.
Is 800 grams more than 1 kilogram, or less?

ask.ifNot: 1 kilogram is a thousand grams. 800 is not quite that many, so it is less than 1 kilogram.

beats.say: 1000 grams make 1 kilogram. 800 is less than 1000, so our answer will start with 0 point something.
To change grams into kilograms we divide by 1000. Each digit slides 3 places to the right.
The 8 lands in the tenths place. 800 divided by 1000 is 0.8.
So 800 grams is 0.8 kilograms.
Check: 0.8 is 8 tenths, and a tenth of a kilogram is 100 grams. 8 of those make 800 grams.
We want to write 80 metres in kilometres.
1000 metres make 1 kilometre. 80 metres is much less than that, so the answer is a small decimal.
To go from metres to kilometres, what do we do?

ask.ifNot: Kilometres are bigger, so we need fewer of them. And 1000 metres make 1 kilometre, so we divide by 1000.

beats.say: 80 divided by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the right. The 8 lands in the hundredths place.
So 80 metres is 0.08 kilometres.
Careful with the place. 0.8 kilometres would be 800 metres, ten times too far.
Divide by 1000, then check where each digit landed.
We want to write 5 milligrams in grams.
How many milligrams make 1 gram?

ask.ifNot: Milli means a thousandth. So 1000 milligrams make 1 gram.

beats.say: 1000 milligrams make 1 gram. So 1 milligram is 1 thousandth of a gram, and we divide by 1000.
5 divided by 1000. The 5 slides 3 places to the right: past the tenths, past the hundredths, into the thousandths.
We fill the empty places with zeros. 0.005.
So 5 milligrams is 0.005 grams.
Thousandths always need 3 places after the point. 0.5 grams would be 500 milligrams, far too much.
3 metres 7 decimetres. We want it all in centimetres.
Start with the metres. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so 3 metres is 300 centimetres.
Now the decimetres. How many centimetres are in 1 decimetre?

ask.ifNot: A decimetre is a tenth of a metre. A tenth of 100 centimetres is 10 centimetres.

beats.say: 1 decimetre is 10 centimetres, so 7 decimetres is 70 centimetres.
Careful: 70, not 7. With 7 centimetres we would get 307, and that is in the choices to catch us.
Add the two parts. 300 plus 70 is 370.
So 3 metres 7 decimetres is 370 centimetres.
3 metres 7 centimetres. This time we want decimetres.
A decimetre sits between the metre and the centimetre. 1 metre is 10 decimetres, and 1 decimetre is 10 centimetres.
The metres first. 3 metres is 3 times 10, which is 30 decimetres.
Now 7 centimetres. Is that more than 1 decimetre, or less?

ask.ifNot: It takes 10 centimetres to make 1 decimetre. We only have 7, so it is less than 1.

beats.say: 7 centimetres is 7 tenths of a decimetre. 7 divided by 10 is 0.7.
Add the parts. 30 plus 0.7 is 30.7.
So 3 metres 7 centimetres is 30.7 decimetres.
Bigger unit to smaller: multiply. Smaller unit to bigger: divide. We used both here.
2.5 kilograms. Let's write it as whole kilograms and grams.
Split at the point. 2 whole kilograms, and 0.5 of a kilogram.
0.5 is the same as a half. 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So what is half a kilogram?

ask.ifNot: Half of 1000 is 500. So half a kilogram is 500 grams.

beats.say: 0.5 times 1000 is 500. So 0.5 kilograms is 500 grams.
So 2.5 kilograms is 2 kilograms 500 grams.
Careful: the 5 after the point does not mean 5 grams. It means 5 tenths of a kilogram.
Split at the point, then multiply the decimal part by 1000.
2.05 litres. Let's write it as whole litres and millilitres.
Split at the point. 2 whole litres, and 0.05 of a litre.
1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So we multiply 0.05 by 1000.
Times 1000 slides the digits 3 places to the left. What does 0.05 become?

ask.ifNot: Slide the 5 once, twice, three times. It ends up in the tens place, with a 0 after it. That makes 50.

beats.say: 0.05 times 1000 is 50. So 0.05 litres is 50 millilitres.
So 2.05 litres is 2 litres 50 millilitres.
Watch that 0 after the point. 0.5 litres would be 500 millilitres, but 0.05 is ten times less.
2.05 metres. Let's write it as whole metres and centimetres.
Split at the point. 2 whole metres, and 0.05 of a metre.
Now be careful. How many centimetres make 1 metre?

ask.ifNot: Centi means a hundredth. So 100 centimetres make 1 metre. The 1000 is for millimetres.

beats.say: 1 metre is 100 centimetres. So we multiply 0.05 by 100, and the digits slide 2 places to the left.
So 0.05 metres is 5 centimetres.
And 2.05 metres is 2 metres 5 centimetres.
With metres and centimetres it is times 100, not times 1000. Know your unit before you multiply.
We want to write 30 kilograms in tonnes. A tonne is a very heavy weight, about as heavy as a small car.
How many kilograms make 1 tonne?

ask.ifNot: A tonne is a thousand kilograms.

beats.say: 1000 kilograms make 1 tonne. 30 kilograms is tiny next to that, so the answer is a small decimal.
We divide by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the right, so the 3 lands in the hundredths place.
So 30 kilograms is 0.03 tonnes.
Check the place. 0.3 tonnes would be 300 kilograms, and 0.003 tonnes would be only 3 kilograms.
Divide by 1000, then check where the digits landed.
A shopkeeper has 5.4 kilograms of rice. He sells 2 kilograms 750 grams. How much rice is left?
One weight is a decimal, and the other is in kilograms and grams. What is the easiest plan?

ask.ifNot: Mixed forms are hard to subtract. If both weights are in grams, it is one simple subtraction.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 5.4 kilograms is 5.4 times 1000, which is 5400 grams.
And 2 kilograms 750 grams is 2000 plus 750, which is 2750 grams.
Now subtract. 5400 minus 2000 is 3400. Then take away the 750: 3400 minus 700 is 2700, and 50 less is 2650.
2650 grams is 2 kilograms and 650 grams. That is how much rice is left.
Check: 2650 plus 2750 is 5400. It works.
The trap is to take 400 from 750 because it looks easier. The 750 is being sold, so it is the one we take away.
A bottle holds 20 litres of water. Each glass takes 300 millilitres. How many glasses can we fill?

board.text: 20 litres. Glasses of 300 ml. How many?

beats.say: Look at the units: litres for the bottle, millilitres for the glasses. So what is our first job?

ask.ifNot: We cannot match litres against millilitres straight away. Let's turn the litres into millilitres, so both are in the same unit.

beats.say: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So 20 litres is 20000 millilitres.
Now, how many lots of 300 fit into 20000? Take two zeros off both numbers. It is the same as 200 divided by 3.
3 times 60 is 180, and 3 times 6 is 18 more. So 3 times 66 is 198. How much of the 200 is left over?

ask.ifNot: Count on from 198 up to 200. That little bit is what is left over.

beats.say: So 66 glasses get filled, and a little water is left. 300 times 66 is 19800, which leaves 200 millilitres.
Careful here: 200 millilitres is not enough for another glass of 300. So we do not count it.
So 66 full glasses can be filled.
Remember: make the units the same first, then see how many full lots fit. A part of a glass does not count.
We have a drum with 10 litres of water, and glasses that hold 250 millilitres each. Let's find how many glasses it fills.

board.text: 10 litres. Glasses of 250 ml. How many?

beats.say: One amount is in litres and the other is in millilitres. What must we do before we share the water out?

ask.ifNot: We cannot match litres against millilitres straight away. Let's turn the litres into millilitres, so both are in the same unit.

beats.say: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So 10 litres is 10000 millilitres.
Now think about just 1 litre, which is 1000 millilitres. How many glasses of 250 does it fill?

ask.ifNot: Count up in steps of 250 until you reach 1000. The number of steps is the number of glasses.

beats.say: 4 glasses of 250 make 1000. So every litre fills 4 glasses.
We have 10 litres, and each one fills 4 glasses. 10 times 4 is 40.
So 40 glasses can be filled.
Let's check. 40 glasses of 250 millilitres make 10000 millilitres. That is the whole drum, so it fits.
Remember: make the units the same first, then see how many lots fit.
A tank holds 10 litres of water. Each glass takes 250 millilitres. How many glasses can we fill?

board.text: 10 litres. Glasses of 250 ml. How many?

beats.say: One amount is in litres and the other is in millilitres. What must we do before we share the water out?

ask.ifNot: We cannot match litres against millilitres straight away. Let's turn the litres into millilitres, so both are in the same unit.

beats.say: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So 10 litres is 10000 millilitres.
Now think about just 1 litre, which is 1000 millilitres. How many glasses of 250 does it fill?

ask.ifNot: Count up in steps of 250 until you reach 1000. The number of steps is the number of glasses.

beats.say: 4 glasses of 250 make 1000. So every litre fills 4 glasses.
We have 10 litres, and each one fills 4 glasses. 10 times 4 is 40.
So 40 glasses can be filled.
Let's check. 40 glasses of 250 millilitres make 10000 millilitres. That is the whole tank, so it fits.
Litres into millilitres first, then share. That plan works for every question like this.
A tank holds 15 litres of water. Each glass takes 500 millilitres. How many glasses can we fill?

board.text: 15 litres. Glasses of 500 ml. How many?

beats.say: Look at the units: litres for the tank, millilitres for the glasses. So what is our first job?

ask.ifNot: We cannot match litres against millilitres straight away. Let's turn the litres into millilitres, so both are in the same unit.

beats.say: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So 15 litres is 15000 millilitres.
Now think about just 1 litre, which is 1000 millilitres. How many glasses of 500 does it fill?

ask.ifNot: Count up in steps of 500 until you reach 1000. The number of steps is the number of glasses.

beats.say: 2 glasses of 500 make 1000. So every litre fills 2 glasses.
We have 15 litres, and each one fills 2 glasses. 15 times 2 is 30.
So 30 glasses can be filled.
Let's check. 30 glasses of 500 millilitres make 15000 millilitres. That is the whole tank, so it fits.
So the plan is: same units first, then count how many glasses fit in.
Here are 4 bags of sugar, and each one weighs 8 kilograms 500 grams. Our job is to find the total weight in grams.

board.text: 4 bags, each 8 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: Each bag's weight mixes two units, kilograms and grams. What is a good first step?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 8 kilograms is 8000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 8500 grams. Careful: 8500 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 4 bags, so we need 8500 times 4. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 8000 times 4?

ask.ifNot: Work out 8 times 4 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 8000 times 4 is 32000. And 500 times 4 is 2000.
Put the two parts together. 32000 plus 2000 makes 34000. So the 4 bags weigh 34000 grams.
So when kilograms and grams are mixed, make it all grams first. Then multiply by the number of bags.
Here are 4 bags of wheat, and each one weighs 2 kilograms 750 grams. Our job is to find the total weight in grams.

board.text: 4 bags, each 2 kg 750 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: The answer has to be in grams, but each bag is given in kilograms and grams. So what shall we do first?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 2 kilograms is 2000 grams.
Now add on the 750 grams. One bag weighs 2750 grams. Careful: 2750 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 4 bags, so we need 2750 times 4. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 2000 times 4?

ask.ifNot: Work out 2 times 4 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 2000 times 4 is 8000. And 750 times 4 is 3000.
Put the two parts together. 8000 plus 3000 makes 11000. So the 4 bags weigh 11000 grams.
The plan to remember: change everything into the small unit first, then multiply.

board.text: 15 litres. Glasses of 250 ml. How many?

beats.say: Look at the units: litres for the drum, millilitres for the glasses. So what is our first job?

ask.ifNot: We cannot match litres against millilitres straight away. Let's turn the litres into millilitres, so both are in the same unit.

beats.say: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So 15 litres is 15000 millilitres.
Now think about just 1 litre, which is 1000 millilitres. How many glasses of 250 does it fill?

ask.ifNot: Count up in steps of 250 until you reach 1000. The number of steps is the number of glasses.

beats.say: 4 glasses of 250 make 1000. So every litre fills 4 glasses.
We have 15 litres, and each one fills 4 glasses. 15 times 4 is 60.
So 60 glasses can be filled.
Let's check. 60 glasses of 250 millilitres make 15000 millilitres. That is the whole drum, so it fits.
Remember: make the units the same first, then see how many lots fit.
Aarav is carrying 4 bags of rice. Every bag weighs 6 kilograms 500 grams. How many grams is that altogether?

board.text: 4 bags, each 6 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: Each bag's weight mixes two units, kilograms and grams. What is a good first step?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 6 kilograms is 6000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 6500 grams. Don't stop here, though. 6500 is just one bag, and it is sitting in the choices to catch us.
There are 4 bags, so we need 6500 times 4. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 6000 times 4?

ask.ifNot: Work out 6 times 4 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 6000 times 4 is 24000. And 500 times 4 is 2000.
Put the two parts together. 24000 plus 2000 makes 26000. So the 4 bags weigh 26000 grams.
So when kilograms and grams are mixed, make it all grams first. Then multiply by the number of bags.
Riya has 2 bags of rice. Each bag weighs 8 kilograms 500 grams. We want the weight of all the bags, in grams.

board.text: 2 bags, each 8 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: The answer has to be in grams, but each bag is given in kilograms and grams. So what shall we do first?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 8 kilograms is 8000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 8500 grams. Careful: 8500 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 2 bags, so we need 8500 times 2. That is doubling. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 8000 times 2?

ask.ifNot: Work out 8 times 2 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 8000 times 2 is 16000. And 500 times 2 is 1000.
Put the two parts together. 16000 plus 1000 makes 17000. So the 2 bags weigh 17000 grams.
Two steps did it: one bag into grams, then times the number of bags. You can use that every time.
A drum holds 5 litres of water. Each glass takes 200 millilitres. How many glasses can we fill?

board.text: 5 litres. Glasses of 200 ml. How many?

beats.say: One amount is in litres and the other is in millilitres. What must we do before we share the water out?

ask.ifNot: We cannot match litres against millilitres straight away. Let's turn the litres into millilitres, so both are in the same unit.

beats.say: 1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So 5 litres is 5000 millilitres.
Now think about just 1 litre, which is 1000 millilitres. How many glasses of 200 does it fill?

ask.ifNot: Count up in steps of 200 until you reach 1000. The number of steps is the number of glasses.

beats.say: 5 glasses of 200 make 1000. So every litre fills 5 glasses.
We have 5 litres, and each one fills 5 glasses. 5 times 5 is 25.
So 25 glasses can be filled.
Let's check. 25 glasses of 200 millilitres make 5000 millilitres. That is the whole drum, so it fits.
Litres into millilitres first, then share. That plan works for every question like this.
Here are 5 bags of lentils, and each one weighs 6 kilograms 500 grams. Our job is to find the total weight in grams.

board.text: 5 bags, each 6 kg 500 g. Total in grams?

beats.say: We want grams at the end. Right now each bag is in kilograms and grams. Where shall we begin?

ask.ifNot: Kilograms and grams are mixed up here. If we turn one bag into grams first, the rest is one easy multiplication.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 6 kilograms is 6000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 6500 grams. Careful: 6500 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 5 bags, so we need 6500 times 5. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 6000 times 5?

ask.ifNot: Work out 6 times 5 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 6000 times 5 is 30000. And 500 times 5 is 2500.
Put the two parts together. 30000 plus 2500 makes 32500. So the 5 bags weigh 32500 grams.
Two steps did it: one bag into grams, then times the number of bags. You can use that every time.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 5 kilograms is 5000 grams.
Now add on the 500 grams. One bag weighs 5500 grams. Careful: 5500 is one of the choices, but that is only one bag.
There are 5 bags, so we need 5500 times 5. Let's do it in two easy parts.
First the thousands. What is 5000 times 5?

ask.ifNot: Work out 5 times 5 first. Then put the three zeros back on the end.

beats.say: 5000 times 5 is 25000. And 500 times 5 is 2500.
Put the two parts together. 25000 plus 2500 makes 27500. So the 5 bags weigh 27500 grams.
